sentence: A 3-year-old male weighing 18 kg was transferred from his hospital of origin for acute renal failure and septic shock (maximum norepinephrine 1 µg/kg/min, mechanical ventilation for 11 days, disseminated intravascular coagulation [DIC], positive blood culture for Streptococcus pyogenes) .
APD was started after 36 hours due to oligoanuria (diuresis of 0.1 ml/kg/h) of 24 hours of evolution, net balance of +1,200 ml and increase in creatinine (initial 0.7 mg/dl, later 2 mg/dl).

On day 1, with ultrafiltration of 685 ml in 24 h, with hourly passes of 12 ml/kg of 1.36% glucose, 20 minutes of residence, the D/P urea and creatinine ratios were 0.73 and 0 .6 respectively, with a Dt/Do glucose of 0.49, so we increased the residence time to 30 minutes and the volume to 17 ml/kg with the same type of liquid and time exchange, since we still had an osmotic gradient: we obtained an increase of daily ultrafiltrate up to 970 ml.
Subsequently, it was necessary to increase the glucose concentration to 3.27% to maintain effective ultrafiltration.

On day 12, with passages every 2 hours of 3.27% fluid, 40 minutes of residence, with 12 ml/kg, the D/P ratios of urea, creatinine and Dt/Do glucose were 0.94, 0.85 and 0.16 respectively, so we decreased the concentration to 2.27% (in such a permeable peritoneum such a hypertonic solution may not be necessary) and increased the permanence to 60 minutes (passes every 2 hours), obtaining ratios of 0 .96, 0.85 and 0.22 respectively (with a less concentrated, less aggressive liquid, we continued to obtain a similar clearance), with a decrease in creatinine in 36 hours from 5.5 mg/dl to 4 mg/dl (kidney function of 8 ml/min/1.73 m2 for urinary creatinine clearance and 10 ml/min/1.73 m2 for Schwarz formula).
On day 15 the cellularity of the dialysate increased and on day 16 the peritoneal catheter was removed (growth of C. albicans).
